chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa from Mansur from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He was asked about a man who sold a sale on credit which he did not possess, and guaranteed the sale. He said, 'There is no objection.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell goods on credit before possessing them in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the sale of a non-existent commodity on credit provided there is a guarantee (*daman*), a ruling that distinguishes it from the stricter prohibition of *bay' al-ma'dum* (sale of what is not present) without such assurance. This permissibility underpins the classical Shia juristic basis for *bay' al-salam* and modern Islamic finance instruments like *ijara wa iqtina*, emphasizing that the guarantee mitigates the uncertainty (*gharar*) inherent in deferred delivery. The ruling highlights the pragmatic approach of the Ahl al-Bayt in facilitating trade while maintaining contractual integrity through clear liability.
